articleTitle: The London Autoguide system (road traffic control)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Car and its Environment - What DRIVE and PROMETHEUS Have to Offer
abstract: However well road users may know London, they are left with the difficulty of choosing the least congested route. They usually never know how successful they have been in relation to possible alternatives. Traffic engineers are faced with a large element of demand which is based on road users random choice. This results in uneven network loading and loss of capacity from conflicting movements which could be avoided. Fuel is wasted, and pollution and driver stress are increased. Here, the author describes the Autoguide system which uses a simple display, backed up by speech messages, giving junction by junction instructions based on optimum routes centrally computed from live traffic information.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: RDS-ALERT: a DRIVE project to develop a proposed standard for the Traffic Message Channel feature of the radio data system RDS
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Car and its Environment - What DRIVE and PROMETHEUS Have to Offer
abstract: RDS-ALERT (Radio Data System-Advice and Problem Location for European Road Traffic) is a project within the European Community's DRIVE research programme. The main goal of this project is to develop, and build European consensus upon, a draft standard for broadcasting traffic messages in densely coded digital form via the proposed Traffic Message Channel (TMC) feature of the radio data system RDS. The author outlines the background to this project, including the existing and proposed capabilities of RDS to assist traffic information broadcasting and gives a brief report on the progress to date.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Car and its Environment - What DRIVE and PROMETHEUS Have to Offer
abstract: PROMETHEUS is a European research programme which will enhance the technical base for road transport. The objective is to create concepts and solutions which will make traffic perceptibly safer, more economical, with less impact on the environment and will make the traffic system more efficient. In this short presentation of this large programme, the author has selected two sub projects, Pro Car and Pro Net, and he describes tests demonstrations that were performed early in 1989 that illustrate a selection of the concepts which are being studied.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Car and its Environment - What DRIVE and PROMETHEUS Have to Offer
abstract: The concept of a head up display (HUD) for automotive use was proposed over 20 years ago and a small number of experimental devices were developed and installed in motor cars for evaluation. An example of this is described by the author. These systems had severe limitations due to the state of development of display technology and automotive instrumentation. However, over the last 15 years HUD's have been developed and used in military aircraft, and the author shows how this technology may be adapted for use in automotive applications.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Car and its Environment - What DRIVE and PROMETHEUS Have to Offer
abstract: Present generation cruise control systems only work well on clear roads and have to be disengaged when it is necessary to change speed because of other traffic. On congested roads the driver is subjected to a high work load maintaining his position relative to the vehicle immediately in front of him. By introducing a sensing system which can determine the distance and relative speeds between a vehicle and the one in front, the author shows that it is possible to develop a cruise control system which will automatically maintain a safe distance between them. He argues that provided a fully automated transmission is fitted, then autonomous intelligent cruise control can give automated stop-start driving in congested urban areas, allowing the driver more time to concentrate on other tasks such as navigating through unfamiliar complex junctions and/or selecting the most appropriate lane.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: MONICA-system integration for incident-congestion detection and traffic monitoring
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Car and its Environment - What DRIVE and PROMETHEUS Have to Offer
abstract: The DRIVE project, MONICA, is being undertaken by a consortium of 10 partners from the UK, France, Germany and Italy with the Transport and Road Research Laboratory, UK, as prime contractors. The author describes the project whose aim is to investigate and develop techniques and systems for the automatic detection of incidents and congestion and for traffic monitoring.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Car and its Environment - What DRIVE and PROMETHEUS Have to Offer
abstract: The acronym PROMETHEUS stands for 'Programme for a European Traffic with Highest Efficiency and Unprecedented Safety', a pre-competitive research programme launched by the European automotive industry. Here, the author deals with co-operative driving as one of the most promising but likewise most challenging concepts to ensure an adequate mobility of individual road users in the future. The basic idea is to provide for intelligent vehicles being able to self-organize their local driving manoeuvres in a co-operative manner without requiring minute guidance and control from traffic management facilities. The expected benefits of this approach are considerably enhanced traffic safety and traffic efficiency as well, where the underlying assumption is that co-operative vehicles have a better perception of and superior operating behaviour in a given traffic environment than individual vehicles driving according to differing autonomous strategies.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: PANDORA-Prototyping A Navigation Database Of Road-network Attributes
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Car and its Environment - What DRIVE and PROMETHEUS Have to Offer
abstract: The author describes the scope and purposes of the PANDORA project in the same terms and provides a brief report on its progress to date. Four European organisations are collaborating on PANDORA: The Automobile Association and Ordnance Survey in the UK, Philips International BV in the Netherlands and Robert Bosch GmbH in West Germany. The project is being managed by consultants MVA Systematics of Woking, who are also providing substantial input in the form of data analysis and software development.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: INVAID-integration of computer vision techniques for automatic incident detection
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Car and its Environment - What DRIVE and PROMETHEUS Have to Offer
abstract: The partners in INVAID represent research, consultancy and manufacturing interests in UK, France, Spain and the Belgium. The INVAID aim is to develop the use of computer vision tools to translate observations in the form of video pictures into traffic condition reports. The particular conditions of interest are incidents and traffic congestion. The overall project and the computer vision tools TITAN and IMPACTS are described by the authors.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
